name: runbook-clear-disk
description: Free disk space on a host without guessing: a report of what fills the filesystem and a written cleanup plan (exact paths and sizes, nothing deleted), human approval of that plan, deletion of exactly the approved paths, and verification of the free space after.

path.description: The mount point or directory that is full.

target_free_pct.description: Free space to reach, in percent.

report.title: What fills the disk
report.prompt:
Host {{input.host}}, path {{input.path}}. Investigate without changing anything: host_stats with disk_usage_path {{input.path}}, and ssh_exec for deeper looks (du -xsk <dir>/*, ls -la <dir>, find, lsof) - ssh_exec runs as the host's read-only account by default, which cannot change it and is not asked about. Classify what you find: safe to delete (caches, temp files, rotated or old logs, core dumps, build leftovers), needs the owner (application data, databases, uploads, backups), and never (anything you cannot identify).
Also record the baseline the verification compares against: probe / ops_check the services on the host now, and note what is already unhealthy before any cleanup (e.g. an expired certificate, a service that cannot be checked).
Write the cleanup plan to .harness/ops/runbooks/clear-disk-plan.md: the current use, then a numbered list of ONLY the safe items, each with the exact path or glob, its size, why it is safe, and the exact command (rm -f / find -delete on that path only, run with ssh_exec as: "operator"). List what you leave alone and why. Do NOT delete anything now.

Report: the use now, the plan's items with sizes, the space they free (in total and as % of the filesystem), and the services' health before the cleanup.

approve.title: Approve the cleanup plan
approve.message:
Free space on {{input.host}} ({{input.path}}) by deleting exactly the items in .harness/ops/runbooks/clear-disk-plan.md?

{{state.report}}

clean.title: Delete the approved items
clean.prompt:
A person approved the cleanup plan .harness/ops/runbooks/clear-disk-plan.md for host {{input.host}}. Read it and delete EXACTLY its listed items with ssh_exec as: "operator" (the read-only account cannot delete), one command per item as written in the plan - nothing that is not in the plan, no wider globs, no other directories. Checks before or after (counts, df) can run as the reader (the default).

Report: each command and its exit status.

verify.title: Verify free space
verify.prompt:
Verify the cleanup on {{input.host}} (read-only): host_stats with disk_usage_path {{input.path}}. The target is at least {{input.target_free_pct}}% free on the filesystem of {{input.path}}; also check that what the plan left alone is still there, and probe/ops_check the services on the host.

Before the cleanup (the baseline, with the services' health then):
{{state.report}}

The cleanup:
{{state.clean}}

VERIFIED when the target is met, what the plan left alone is intact, and nothing is worse than in the baseline. A problem that was already there before the cleanup, or that a disk cleanup cannot cause (an expired certificate, a service the tools cannot check), does not fail it: list it as pre-existing, for its own ticket. FAILED when the target is not met, something the plan kept is gone, or a service became unhealthy after the cleanup.

Report: free space before and after, the checks, and any pre-existing problems.
